solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Phone company about Sarah's mobile in general, say

indicators.note: about means the company's letters go round the rest

parts.note: BT is British Telecom, the UK's main phone company

indicators.note: mobile means moving freely, so the letters of Sarah's are rearranged

explanation.surface: A telephone firm seems to be dealing with Sarah's mobile phone, in a general way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mobile' looks like the phone itself, but it is the anagram signal, and 'about' wraps the phone company round the result. 'say' marks the general as one example of the class.
explanation.definitionFit: A brass hat is British slang for a high-ranking officer, of which a general is one example.

clue.text: The Dandy covers half your desk

indicators.note: covers means the dandy's word is wrapped round the other piece

parts.note: a beau is a dandy, a fashionable man

indicators.note: half takes the last two of the four letters

explanation.surface: A copy of The Dandy comic covers half of your desk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Dandy' looks like the British children's comic, but the dandy is a beau, wrapped round UR.
explanation.definitionFit: A bureau is a writing desk with drawers and a sloping lid.

clue.text: Oxygen extracted from alternative plant fertiliser

indicators.note: extracted from means the element is pulled out of the word

parts.note: another means an alternative one
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: Oxygen is extracted from an alternative fertiliser for plants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fertiliser' reads as manure, but the definition is the pollen-bearing organ of a flower, which fertilises the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The anther is the part of a stamen that bears pollen, the agent of fertilisation in flowering plants.

clue.text: I fasten folds round baby's bottom softly

definitions.text: I fasten folds round baby's bottom softly

indicators.note: round means the anagram goes around the other letters
folds means the letters are bent into a new shape
bottom takes the last letter of the word for baby

parts.note: P is piano, the musical marking for softly

explanation.surface: The pin itself speaks: it secures the folds of a nappy round a baby's bottom, gently.
explanation.walkthrough: SAFETIN from 'I fasten' goes round Y and P; the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A safety pin, with its guarded point, is the classic fastener for a cloth nappy.

clue.text: I call up directors about clubs after article in press

indicators.note: after puts the rest following the article

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
to ring is to telephone, to call
C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs
taken as written
a company's directors are its board

explanation.surface: Someone calls up the directors about their clubs after an article appears in the press.
explanation.walkthrough: 'press' looks like the newspapers, but it is the definition: in Scotland and Ireland a press is a cupboard. 'about' is loose placement, setting the clubs letter in front.
explanation.definitionFit: A press is a cupboard for linen or clothes, and an airing cupboard is a warm one for drying laundry.

clue.text: Book one has returned with excellent contents

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: contents means the next piece is held inside the reversed word
returned means the word has is written back to front

parts.note: taken as written
A1 means first-rate, written AI in crosswords

explanation.surface: A book, one that has come back with excellent material inside it, as from a library.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns the word round, giving SAH; A1, written AI, is the crossword shorthand for first-rate, and 'contents' puts it inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Isaiah is a prophetic book of the Old Testament, so it is one example of a biblical book.

clue.text: On which, left out, she'll finish primarily?

definitions.text: On which, left out, she'll finish primarily?

indicators.note: out means the letter is left out of the word
primarily takes the first letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: An unmarried woman, overlooked, may end up there.
explanation.walkthrough: SHEL (she'll less one L) plus F; 'on the shelf' is an old idiom for someone left unmarried.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on the shelf means being passed over, as of an unmarried woman considered past marriageable age.

clue.text: Setter's hosting exotic ladies, hoping for the best

indicators.note: hosting means the setter's word holds the next piece

parts.note: the setter is I, so setter's is I'm, short for I am

indicators.note: exotic means strange or foreign, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A setter entertains exotic ladies, hoping for the best.
explanation.walkthrough: Crossword setters refer to themselves as I or me, so 'Setter's' is I'M; 'exotic' scrambles the ladies to DEALIS and 'hosting' holds them inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Idealism is the habit of believing in high ideals and expecting the best outcome.

clue.text: Individual with yen to dip into wild hebe?

definitions.text: Individual with yen to dip into wild hebe?

indicators.note: to dip into means those pieces go inside the scrambled letters
wild means uncontrolled, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: one is a single individual
Y is the symbol for the yen, Japan's currency

explanation.surface: A creature that longs to dip into the flowers of a wild hebe shrub.
explanation.walkthrough: A hebe is a flowering evergreen shrub; ONEY goes inside BEEH after its first letter H.
explanation.definitionFit: Honeybees forage for nectar by dipping into flowers such as those of the hebe.

clue.text: Sore throat throbbing? It is a problem of articulation

indicators.note: throbbing means pulsing, so the letters are thrown about

explanation.surface: A throbbing sore throat makes it hard to speak clearly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'articulation' suggests speech, but it means the joints; 'It is' stands unchanged at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Osteoarthritis is degeneration of the joints, and joints are articulations in anatomy.

clue.text: Swimmer in Roaring Forties almost at end of tether

indicators.note: roaring suggests wild, tumultuous movement, so the letters are churned up
almost means the word loses its final letter
end of picks the last letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Someone swimming in the stormy Roaring Forties of the Southern Ocean is nearly at the end of their tether.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roaring Forties' reads as the stormy latitudes, but 'Roaring' is the anagram signal: FORTIE (Forties without its S, from 'almost') becomes ROTIFE, then R from 'tether' follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotifers are microscopic aquatic animals that propel themselves with whirling cilia, so a tiny swimmer.

clue.text: Man with barrels spotted casing speakeasy

indicators.note: casing means the word for spotted wraps around the other pieces

parts.note: spotted means seen
man gives the pronoun he

explanation.surface: A man with beer barrels was seen at the door of an illegal drinking den.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spotted' reads as describing the man but is the word wrapped round the others; 'casing' signals the wrapping.
explanation.definitionFit: A shebeen is an Irish or South African unlicensed drinking house, the same thing as a Prohibition-era speakeasy.

clue.text: Factor in mature property custodians

parts.note: to mature is to age
NT is the National Trust, the British charity that looks after historic houses and land

explanation.surface: A consideration in looking after mature properties held by custodians.
explanation.walkthrough: The National Trust is a British conservation charity that owns and cares for historic properties.
explanation.definitionFit: A factor, in the old commercial sense, is someone who acts for another in business, which is an agent.

clue.text: Fuelled stove in city as required

indicators.note: in means the scrambled letters sit inside the city

parts.note: NY is New York

indicators.note: stove is the past tense of stave in, meaning smashed, so the word is broken up

explanation.surface: A stove in some city is fuelled as needed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stove' looks like a cooker, but it is the past tense of stave in, smashed: the anagram signal, giving EEDFULL, which 'in' places inside the city.
explanation.definitionFit: Done needfully means done out of necessity, which is to say as required.

clue.text: Unusual supplement sadly causes piles, I gathered

indicators.note: sadly here means in a sorry state, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A one-off supplement, I'm told, unfortunately causes piles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I gathered' adds a gossipy aside; only the I is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A special issue of a magazine is an extra, out-of-the-ordinary edition, hence an unusual supplement.

clue.text: I make an impression with one brief visit in uniform

parts.note: to dent is to press a hollow into something
one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: brief means the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: to call is to pay a visit

explanation.surface: A person makes a good impression on a short visit, dressed in uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uniform' is not a dress code here but means all the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that are uniform are exactly alike, with no variation between them.

clue.text: Impressions of oriental objects enthral Chinese leader

parts.note: E stands for east, oriental

indicators.note: enthral means to hold captive, so the objects hold the next letter

parts.note: objects are things

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Pictures of oriental objects captivate a Chinese leader.
explanation.walkthrough: C goes inside THINGS after its T, with E in front.
explanation.definitionFit: An etching is a print taken from an etched plate, so an impression in the printmaking sense.

clue.text: Offensive Conservative politician gets in again after bruising

indicators.note: gets in means the politician is placed inside the scrambled word
after bruising means the word has been knocked about

parts.note: MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A rude Conservative politician gets elected again after a bruising contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Offensive' reads as rude but is a noun, a military push; 'after bruising' scrambles the repeat word to AAIGN, and 'gets in' places the politician inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A campaign is a planned series of military operations, the same as an offensive.

clue.text: Welsh character coaches snooker player

parts.note: railway coaches make up trains
a potter is one who pots balls, as a snooker player does

explanation.surface: A Welsh person coaches a snooker player.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Welsh' is not Wales: Irvine Welsh wrote the novel Trainspotting, whose characters include a trainspotter.
explanation.definitionFit: Irvine Welsh's novel Trainspotting takes its title from the hobby, and a railway enthusiast appears in it as a character.

clue.text: In the meantime, this inn could become prominent

indicators.note: could become means the letters can be rearranged; with the inn's letters added they would make the longer word

explanation.surface: A local inn might turn into a prominent place.
explanation.walkthrough: PROMINENT minus the letters of INN leaves PROTEM, rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Pro tem is short for the Latin pro tempore, for the time being.

clue.text: Trainer whipped his pony? That's not new

indicators.note: whipped means beaten about, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A trainer whipped his pony, but that's nothing new.
explanation.walkthrough: HISPONY less N, from 'That's not new', is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A physio is a physiotherapist, and sports teams use them as fitness trainers.

clue.text: Chance upon youth hostel initially in rain? Drink's cheap in it

parts.note: hap is an old word for chance or luck

indicators.note: in means those initial letters sit inside the word for rain

parts.note: to pour is to rain heavily

indicators.note: initially takes the first letters of the two words

explanation.surface: A traveller comes across a youth hostel in the rain and finds drinks are cheap there.
explanation.walkthrough: Hap is an archaic word for luck; 'upon' simply joins it to what follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Happy hour is the period when a bar sells alcohol at reduced prices, so cheap drinking time.

clue.text: Swift brute throws grass over middle of room

indicators.note: over in a down clue means the word is turned upside down

parts.note: hay is dried grass

indicators.note: middle of takes the central letters of the word

explanation.surface: A swift animal hurls grass across the middle of a room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swift' is Jonathan Swift: in Gulliver's Travels the Yahoos are brutish humans.
explanation.definitionFit: In Gulliver's Travels Jonathan Swift's Yahoos are degraded, bestial humans, hence a brute of his invention.

clue.text: Electric Light Orchestra, the second pair masking the first

indicators.note: masking means the answer is concealed within the second pair of words

explanation.surface: Reads as a note about the band Electric Light Orchestra.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue explains itself: the second pair of words, 'Light Orchestra', conceals the meaning of the first pair, 'Electric Light'.
explanation.definitionFit: In British English a torch is a battery-powered handheld lamp, which is an electric light.

clue.text: Doctor in there implying both options are ruled out

definitions.text: implying both options are ruled out

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so the letters are altered

explanation.surface: A doctor in there implies that both treatment options are excluded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' reads as a physician but is a verb signalling the anagram of IN THERE.
explanation.definitionFit: The word rejects each of two alternatives, as in 'neither this nor that'.

clue.text: "The Quiet American" or "The History Man"?

parts.note: tacit means unspoken or silent

explanation.surface: Two novel titles, Greene's The Quiet American and Bradbury's The History Man, offered as alternatives.
explanation.walkthrough: Both titles are real novels; the first is the wordplay, the second the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacitus was a Roman historian, so literally a history man.

clue.text: Local star in person celebrated party in retreat

parts.note: sung means praised or celebrated in song

indicators.note: in retreat means the word goes backwards

parts.note: a do is a party

explanation.surface: A local celebrity appears in person at a party held at a retreat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Local star' is our own star, the sun, and 'in person' means personified.
explanation.definitionFit: A deity embodying the sun is our nearest star given personal form, as with Ra or Helios.

clue.text: Neapolitan hit: "I love to finish old unfinished grave"

indicators.note: to finish puts the following pieces at the very end
unfinished means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: grave means serious or solemn
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A singer quotes a famous Naples song about finishing an old, unfinished grave.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads O, SOLEM, then 'I love' placed last as IO.
explanation.definitionFit: O Sole Mio is the celebrated Neapolitan song of 1898, a hit for many tenors.
